Umbrasas / LRT Water tourism is enjoying a surge in popularity in Lithuania, with both domestic travellers and foreign visitors increasingly choosing holidays built around the countryâs thousands of lakes and rivers. According to the national tourism promotion agency Travel Lithuania, about 60% of Lithuanians spend their summer vacations near lakes, rivers or the Baltic Sea. âWater tourism is becoming increasingly popular around the world,â said Jolanta MasiulienÄ, a representative of Travel Lithuania. âPeople no longer want just to swim. They want to be on the water, travel on the water and experience it.â Lithuania offers plenty of opportunities to do just that. The country is home to more than 3,000 lakes and roughly twice as many rivers, supporting activities ranging from kayaking and paddleboarding to recreational diving and nighttime excursions. Diving finds a younger generation At a lakeside diving centre in MolÄtai, founder Martynas Ulinskas says one of the most encouraging trends has been the growing interest among children and teenagers. Kayaking | J. StaceviÄius / LRT âWhat makes me happiest is seeing children actively take up this activity and replace time spent on computers and phones with time underwater,â he said. Unlike many outdoor pursuits, scuba diving is less dependent on the weather, allowing enthusiasts to continue exploring beneath the surface even when summer skies turn grey. Campground operators, however, say this yearâs unsettled weather has affected visitor numbers. âWe usually consider summer to begin after the Midsummer holiday,â said Romualdas Spunis, manager of a campground in MindÅ«nai. âThe first or second weekend is normally when the entire campground is fully booked, but there havenât been many such weekends this year. When it rains, nature isnât as attractive a destination.â Shorter adventures, broader appeal Kayaking remains Lithuaniaâs most popular water activity, according to tourism operators, although visitors are increasingly looking for shorter, more flexible routes. Instead of spending several days paddling downstream, many now prefer trips lasting only a few hours that combine rivers and lakes. Kayaking | J. StaceviÄius / LRT âYou can still fish from a pier, but people rent boats, kayaks and increasingly paddleboards because they want to try something new,â Spunis said. Lithuaniaâs extensive network of interconnected lakes has helped diversify those experiences, offering routes suitable for beginners as well as more experienced paddlers. Foreign visitors discover Lithuaniaâs waters Domestic travellers still account for the overwhelming majority of visitors at many lakeside destinations. About 90% of tourists in the MolÄtai region are Lithuanians, according to Daiva KulienÄ, director of the MolÄtai Tourism and Business Information Centre. Among international visitors, Dutch and German tourists remain regular guests at local campgrounds, while Poland has emerged as a growing market. The Green Lakes in Vilnius | D. Umbrasas / LRT âPeople from our region often travel to the Baltic coast, while visitors from KlaipÄda come to the lake district,â KulienÄ said. Among international visitors, Dutch and German tourists remain regular guests at local campgrounds, she added, while Poland has emerged as a growing market. Travel Lithuania says, however, that French, American and Latvian visitors have been among the most enthusiastic international users of Lithuaniaâs water tourism offerings. https://nineoclock.ro/romania-budget-def.text: ABOUT US NINE O’CLOCK STAFF 2024 COMMERCIAL OFFER – 2026 Subscribe to the Nine O’Clock 2026 CONTACT Special price offer 2026 with a 50% discount Romania Budget Deficit Falls by 37% in Seven Months as Investment Spending Rises 24% Finance Minister Alexandru Nazare Romania’s budget deficit narrowed sharply in the first seven months of 2026, falling by RON 28.36 billion compared with the same period last year, while public investment continued to expand, according to figures released by the Ministry of Finance on Monday. The consolidated general budget posted a deficit of RON 48.08 billion in January-July, compared with RON 76.44 billion a year earlier. The deficit fell by 37% in nominal terms, while its share of GDP declined to 2.34% from 3.99%, an improvement of 1.65 percentage points. The fiscal adjustment was supported by stronger revenue collection and a slower increase in public spending. Total budget revenues rose 11.2% year-on-year to RON 412.31 billion, while expenditure increased by just 2.9% to RON 460.39 billion. At the same time, investment spending increased by approximately 24% to RON 76.51 billion, RON 14.83 billion more than in the same period of 2025. “Data for the first seven months show that we are consistently maintaining the trend of reducing the budget deficit and stabilising public finances. The 1.65 percentage point reduction in the deficit is evidence of balanced management, combining fiscal responsibility with direct support for the economy. We continued VAT reimbursements without interruption, returning more than RON 20.4 billion to companies to provide them with the liquidity they need, and directed resources as a priority towards the main development pillars, where investment from European funds and the NRRP increased by more than 60%. As we consolidate this healthier foundation for public finances, the next step is to turn stabilisation into healthy and sustainable economic growth, ” Finance Minister Alexandru Nazare said. Revenue growth drives fiscal adjustment Total revenues reached RON 412.31 billion in the first seven months, up 11.2% year-on-year. Tax revenues increased by 15.4% to RON 214.32 billion, while their share of GDP rose from 9.69% to 10.42%. Net VAT revenues climbed 26.5% year-on-year to RON 88.55 billion. Gross VAT receipts increased by 21.7%, partly reflecting the new VAT rates introduced under Law No. 141/2025. VAT refunds to the private sector also increased by 4.6%, reaching RON 20.48 billion. Excise revenues amounted to RON 28.37 billion, up 6.4% compared with the same period last year, driven particularly by a 10.9% increase in revenues from energy products. EU reimbursements for eligible expenditure and grants rose 30.3% to RON 37.28 billion. Revenue from personal income and wage taxes totalled RON 38.34 billion, up 8.6% year-on-year. Corporate income tax receipts increased by 8.3% to RON 28.35 billion, while social security contributions rose 6.7% to RON 129.14 billion. Public spending rises at a slower pace Total expenditure amounted to RON 460.39 billion, representing a 2.9% nominal increase from the first seven months of 2025. As a share of GDP, however, public spending declined from 23.3% to 22.4%. Personnel spending fell 4.1% year-on-year to RON 95.67 billion, equivalent to 4.7% of GDP. The government attributed the decline to reductions in certain allowances and wage restraint measures. Personnel spending also accounted for a smaller share of total expenditure, falling from 22.3% to 20.8%. Spending on goods and services increased 11.2% to RON 59.6 billion, mainly due to higher payments in the healthcare system. Interest expenditure remained a significant pressure on the budget, rising 26.5% year-on-year to RON 40.12 billion, equivalent to 2% of GDP. The government said continued fiscal consolidation is intended to reduce financing needs and, over the medium term, limit pressure from public debt servicing costs. Social assistance spending declined 0.6% to RON 146.59 billion, while subsidies totalled RON 7.51 billion. Investment spending rises despite deficit reduction Investment expenditure reached RON 76.51 billion in January-July, up RON 14.83 billion, or approximately 24%, from the same period last year. Projects financed through non-reimbursable external funds accounted for RON 45.88 billion. Payments for projects backed by non-reimbursable external funds increased 39.1%, while expenditure related to the grant component of the NRRP more than doubled year-on-year. Around 71.05% of total investment spending was represented by projects supported through European funds and the NRRP, including grants and loans. Payments under these financing lines increased by RON 20.40 billion, or 60.08%, year-on-year. Nazare said the investment figures showed that the reduction in the deficit had not been achieved by halting development spending, but through tighter control of current expenditure and stronger revenue collection. Government warns of tougher comparisons ahead Nazare said the latest budget execution figures represented an important signal for investors and financial markets, but cautioned that the pace of improvement seen so far should be interpreted in the context of the measures adopted last year. “The results after seven months send an important signal of stability and fiscal responsibility. Romania is strengthening its credibility both externally and domestically, and this is a very important signal for markets, investors, and confidence in the Romanian economy. A country that conveys confidence and fiscal consistency is a stronger country. However, we must also interpret the budget executions of the coming months correctly. From August, the annualised effects of the measures adopted in July 2025 will become visible, meaning that the comparison base will change and the differences versus last year will naturally narrow. What matters is maintaining budget execution within the planned profile and on the trajectory required to meet the full-year deficit target. The next stage is to ensure that the fiscal adjustment becomes structural and sustainable. Maintaining expenditure discipline, a predictable wage policy, accelerating the absorption of European funds, and prioritising investment are essential components for continuing this trajectory,” Nazare added. Nazare also pointed to S&P’s upcoming assessment of Romania as the next major test for the country’s fiscal credibility. He said the seven-month budget execution would support the government’s discussions with rating agencies, but warned that markets and investors would continue to scrutinise Romania’s ability to maintain the current fiscal trajectory and present a credible budget for 2027. The finance minister also stressed that fiscal credibility can be lost quickly, particularly while financing costs remain high, making further credible deficit reduction important for companies and the wider economy. https://www.euronews.com/2026/09/21/us-h.text: The United States has deported more than 25,000 people under secretive agreements with 35 countries to take migrants with no ties to those nations, according to an investigation published on Monday.Since US President Donald Trump took office in January 2025, Washington has been signing deals with developing countries to take migrants who cannot legally be sent home.The investigation by Forbidden Stories found the administration has earmarked $410 million (€357 million) to be paid directly to the receiving countries or to UN agencies to facilitate the returns.At least 25,447 people had already been deported to third countries by 31 August 2026, according to data compiled by Forbidden Stories with a consortium of international journalists.The vast majority, around 20,000, were sent to Mexico, but the rest were dispersed to 27 other countries across Latin America, Africa and the Pacific, and agreements have been finalised with seven more.The deals vary, including over which nationalities can be deported and whether people with criminal records can be accepted.An investigation by the AFP news agency earlier this year found Washington is using visa bans and restrictions on African countries to strongarm them into accepting deportees.Lawyers told AFP that deportees were being thrown into a "legal black hole," held without charge in countries where they have no ties and few if any rights.Forbidden Stories said 49 of Africa's 54 countries had been approached about accepting third-country deportees.A little-known State Department division called the Office of Remigration, created in May 2025, has handled most of the negotiations and payments, according to Forbidden Stories.The office is headed by Christian Jove Ehrhardt, a 41-year-old diplomat who previously worked as a security officer.The report details his visits to Cameroon, which signed a memorandum of understanding with the US in December on accepting deportees. A week later, it also signed a five-year health assistance programme worth nearly $400 million (€348 million).The following month, the State Department said it would provide a further $30 million (€26 million) to the UN Refugee Agency (UNHCR) in Cameroon to "facilitate the voluntary return of refugees and combat illegal immigration."The first plane carrying deportees arrived in Cameroon on 14 January.PaymentsOther agreements have involved direct payments to governments.Palau, a small Pacific island nation with a population of under 18,000, signed an agreement in December 2025 to accept up to 75 third-country nationals in return for $7.5 million (€6.5 million).However, only three people have so far been sent under the agreement.In Eswatini, 32 people have arrived since July 2025 out of a possible 160 under an agreement worth more than $5 million (€4 million). It has accepted deportees with criminal records, the investigation found.Of the $410 million planned for the agreements, internal State Department records showed that $81 million (€70 million) was earmarked for signatory governments.The rest was intended for aid organisations, including more than $178 million (€155 million) for the UN's International Organisation for Migration and $123 million (€107 million) for UNHCR.The agencies have faced criticism over their involvement, although UNHCR told Forbidden Stories that it was not party to the bilateral agreements and that US funding was being used in line with its mandate to strengthen asylum systems.An IOM spokesperson told Forbidden Stories that the agency's decisions to accept funding rested "on a single question: whether our engagement will improve the lives of the migrants affected. In these instances, we believe strongly it does."

https://www.aol.co.uk/articles/nato-figh.text: Rucsandra Moldoveanu Updated Mon, September 14, 2026 at 8:07 AM UTC 0 NATO fighter jets have been scrambled in Lithuania (stock) -Credit:Getty Images An international airport was closed in the capital of Lithuania after what was believed to be a drone sighting - but the actual cause was much less serious. NATO fighter jets were scrambled in Vilnius, Lithuania , as residents received text message alerts. All flights from Vilnius International Airport were suspended during the operation on Sunday. The yellow alert, issued by LT72 - Lithuania's emergency platform - was sent out at around 1pm local time (11am BST). It read: "AIR RAID ALERT (YELLOW). Potentially detected drone. Find a safe place. If you see a suspicious object, keep away, call 112. Wait for the all-clear." The alert was sent out to those in Vilnius city, Elektrėnai district, Trakai district and Vilnius district. It was in place for just under 40 minutes. • NATO fighter jets scrambled over Europe as emergency alert issued in Poland • Putin holds three-hour Kremlin talks with Trump envoys on ending Ukraine war Flights at Vilnius International Airport have now resumed. Vilmantas Vitkauskas, head of the National Crisis Management Center, told LRT radio: "People can calm down. (...) In principle, the threat level has been eliminated." After the situation was dealt with, residents in Vilnius received an alert stating: "The Lithuanian Armed Forces inform: air alert is over. You may leave safe places or shelters." This morning, the Lithuanian military said that Air Force radars near Varena had detected a target, thought to be a drone, moving in the direction of Kaliningrad and had likely entered Lithuania from Belarus . The military later said: "After the radar tag left Lithuanian airspace, there was no reason to declare an air alert." But it has now been determined that the unidentified object was actually a flock of birds, 15min reports . The National Crisis Management Center stated: "Fighter jets carrying out a NATO air policing mission were deployed to inspect the object. "They determined that the radar signals were a flock of birds. In the initial radar information, the markings of birds and drones may be similar, therefore, an additional check was carried out to accurately determine the nature of the object." Photograph: Frederic J Brown/AFP/Getty Images Georgia Five people shot and killed in apparent murder-suicide, Georgia police say Deceased were all members of the same family, officials say, and one of victims placed the initial emergency call Uwa Ede-Osifo Sat 10 Oct 2026 20.01 EDT Last modified on Sat 10 Oct 2026 20.04 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google Five people were shot and killed in an apparent murder-suicide at a residence in Georgia on Friday, authorities say. The deceased were family members who lived at the home in Douglas, a city in south Georgia . Officers responded to reports of an active shooter later on Friday, Brannen Pruette, the Douglas police chief, said at a Saturday news conference. One of the victims placed the initial emergency call. Responding officers found four deceased adults inside the home. A fifth individual was transported to a hospital, where they were later pronounced dead. Nine people, including children, dead after mass shooting in Pennsylvania Read more Details around how the tragedy unfolded remain unclear, including who opened fire. Hours before the deadly shooting, a female victim called police to complain that her husband was “killing her” with his smoking. EMS transported her to a local medical center. Police did not offer additional information, citing the ongoing investigation. “We recognize the profound impact this loss has on those closest to the victims in our community. We ask everyone to respect the privacy of the family and allow them the time and space they need to grieve,” Pruette said. Charlie Davis, the Douglas city manager, said it was the area’s second murder-suicide incident in three months. skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Around 2-3 times a day Sign up to Breaking News US Get the most important news as it breaks after newsletter promotion “Domestic violence doesn’t know race. It doesn’t know religion. It doesn’t know geographic location,” Davis said. “We encourage everyone to refrain from speculation and allow the family the space, dignity and compassion they deserve during this time.” In a similar episode of violence, a man in Pennsylvania fatally shot several family members on Friday, before killing himself. https://www.dw.com/en/germany-arrests-uk.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5OY21 The suspect is expected to be brought before a judge on Friday Image: Uli Deck/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement Police in the German state of Brandenburg have arrested a Ukrainian man on suspicion of spying for Russia , the Federal Public Prosecutor's Office in Karlsruhe said Thursday. The man, identified only as Vadym Y. by prosecutors, is suspected of having used his connections to European defense firms to gather information that he then allegedly passed on to a Russian spy agency. What do we know about the alleged espionage in Germany? Prosecutors said he had been in touch with a middleman since July 2025. They said he had been gathering intelligence in connection with the Russian full-scale invasion of Ukraine from Germany. This information reportedly included "details regarding the production of armored vehicles, ammunition and explosives, as well as information on personnel and military facilities at locations intended to secure NATO's eastern flank." Germany has been on high alert for acts of sabotage in recent months, especially since an explosive-laden drone was discovered near a Ukrainian cargo plane at Leipzig airport. Berlin said Moscow was behind the attempted attack. Germany gives spy agencies expanded powers To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Why is Germany worried about Russia's 'hybrid' war? Germany is one of the biggest military and political supporters of Ukraine, especially following an increasingly friendly US stance toward Russia under President Donald Trump. This seems to have put Germany in Russia's crosshairs as part of what has been called a "hybrid" campaign of espionage, sabotage and other disruptions. German Chancellor Friedrich Merz said he was not surprised by the arrest, adding that there would be more such cases ⁠in ​the future. Besides the incident at Leipzig airport, there have been numerous cases of people being arrested on suspicion of spying for Russia. Moscow has denied all allegations. This has led Germany to give increased powers to its own spying agency, the BND. The agency's chief, Martin Jaeger, told German lawmakers earlier in October that the Russian "shadow war" is escalating and has "taken on a new, more dangerous character." "Germany is at risk of being drawn into a violent conflict with Russia," he told a hearing of parliament's intelligence oversight committee in Berlin.
